name: Requirement ↔ Test Matrix
blurb: each requirement matched with the test that proves it, gaps shown
intro: A requirements traceability matrix: every requirement traced to the tests (or inspection and analysis records) that prove it, with the gaps, failures and orphan tests listed. Coverage follows the bidirectional traceability of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148; the list is saved as the project's record in the app.

default.text: Fan speed set in 10 steps with the encoder
Board fits a 50 x 30 mm outline
USB port survives ±8 kV contact ESD (IEC 61000-4-2)

inputs.label: Tests and verification records
inputs.help: Covers: the requirement IDs this test proves, separated by commas or spaces.

default.name: ESD gun on the USB shield and pins
Standby current with a µA meter

usage: Pass `reqs` as rows {id, text, priority: must|should|could, method: test|analysis|inspection|demonstration} and `tests` as rows {id, name, covers: 'REQ-01, REQ-02', result: 'not run'|pass|fail|blocked}. It returns coverage and verified percentages, the matrix with a status per requirement (no evidence, failing, blocked, not run, partly run, verified), a requirement x test grid when there are 12 tests or fewer, a Markdown matrix, and warnings for must-have gaps, failures, unknown IDs and tests that cover nothing. The project's lists are read or written with the MCP tool tool_data (id req-test-matrix, data {reqs: [...], tests: [...]}).
sources: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 Systems and software engineering - Requirements engineering (bidirectional traceability, verification)
INCOSE Systems Engineering Handbook, 5th ed. - verification methods: inspection, analysis, demonstration, test
